paragraphs.title: The Destruction of the Cities and Moab's Mourning

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that Ar of Moab and Kir of Moab were laid waste in the night.
easy.q: Which two cities are said to have been laid waste at the beginning of the passage?

answers: By wearing sackcloth, wailing, and weeping
easy.explanation: The passage describes baldness, cut beards, sackcloth, howling, and abundant weeping.
easy.q: How did the people of Moab express their mourning?

answers: In the streets and on the tops of their houses
easy.explanation: Verse 3 places the mourning in the streets and on the tops of the houses.
easy.q: Where did the people mourn and howl?

answers: The destruction of Ar and Kir
medium.explanation: The mourning follows the destruction of the Moabite cities of Ar and Kir.
medium.q: What caused Moab's deep mourning in these verses?

answers: A practice of mourning involving the shaving of the head
A sign that the people were preparing for battle
A celebration held in the city
medium.explanation: Baldness in this context is a visible sign of grief and mourning.
medium.q: What does the phrase “on all their heads shall be baldness” indicate?

answers: It was limited to one family
It affected the public life of the whole community
medium.explanation: The mourning is shown in homes, on rooftops, and throughout the streets.
medium.q: What does the movement from houses to streets show about the mourning?

answers: The destruction leads to widespread public mourning
The destruction leads to a joyful celebration
The destruction has no effect on the people
challenge.explanation: The fallen cities lead the people to shave their heads, wear sackcloth, howl, and weep.
challenge.q: What connection does the passage make between the destruction of the cities and the people's response?

answers: Several cities are mentioned and people mourn in many public places
The people show no reaction to the event
challenge.explanation: Ar and Kir are named, while mourning is heard and seen throughout the community.
challenge.q: Why can the disaster be understood as more than a local event?

answers: A peaceful city preparing for a feast
A society devastated by destruction and mourning openly
challenge.explanation: The ruined cities and public grief present Moab as a community overwhelmed by disaster.
challenge.q: Which description best summarizes Moab's condition in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Cry of Distress and the Flight of the Refugees

easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that Heshbon and Elealeh cry, and their voice is heard unto Jahaz.
easy.q: Which cities cry out, and whose voice is heard even unto Jahaz?

answers: They flee and go up the road with weeping
They return to the ruined cities
They stop all cries of distress
easy.explanation: The fugitives flee unto Zoar and go up the way with weeping.
The passage says that in the way of Horonaim they raise up a cry of destruction.
easy.q: What is raised up in the way of Horonaim?

answers: The cries accompany the people's flight from disaster
The cries prevent the people from leaving
medium.explanation: The cries of the cities and the weeping fugitives are presented as parts of the same calamity.
medium.q: How are the cries of the cities related to the flight of the refugees?

medium.explanation: The KJV identifies these people as the armed soldiers of Moab.
medium.q: In the phrase “the armed soldiers of Moab,” who are being described?

answers: The event was hidden from everyone
The distress was severe and spread over a wide area
The cities had always been empty
medium.explanation: A cry heard from afar emphasizes both the intensity and the extent of the suffering.
medium.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the voice is heard even unto Jahaz?

answers: With sorrow and a cry of grief
challenge.explanation: The prophet says, “My heart shall cry out for Moab,” showing deep sorrow.
challenge.q: How does the prophet respond to Moab's condition?

answers: Both the people remaining and those fleeing are affected by the disaster
The fugitives have defeated their enemies
challenge.explanation: The soldiers cry out while the fugitives flee and weep, showing widespread suffering.
challenge.q: What does the combination of the soldiers' cry and the fugitives' weeping suggest?

answers: Crying cities, a cry of distress, flight, and weeping
challenge.explanation: The verses move from the cries of Heshbon and Elealeh to distress, flight, and weeping.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the events in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Desolation, Loss of Property, and Continuing Calamity

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate.
easy.q: What happens to the waters of Nimrim?

answers: The hay withers, and the grass and green things fail
easy.explanation: The verse describes withered hay, failing grass, and the absence of anything green.
Verse 9 says that the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood.
easy.q: What are the waters of Dimon said to contain?

answers: They remain safely in the houses
They are carried away to the brook of the willows
They are returned to their owners
medium.explanation: Verse 7 says that what they have gotten and laid up shall be carried away.
medium.q: What happens to the abundance and stored goods of the Moabites?

medium.explanation: The word describes a barren and ruined condition.
medium.q: In this context, what does “desolate” mean?

answers: They strengthen the picture of desolation and calamity
They signal that the danger has ended
medium.explanation: The loss of water and vegetation emphasizes the land's devastation.
medium.q: How do the dried waters and failed vegetation contribute to the passage?

answers: The disaster is limited to one city
The distress spreads across a broad region
The borders have become a place of rest
challenge.explanation: The howling reaches from Eglaim to Beerelim, surrounding Moab's borders.
challenge.q: What does the cry extending around the borders of Moab show?

answers: The waters fail, property is carried away, Dimon's waters fill with blood, and escapees face lions
The waters increase, property is protected, and the cities become peaceful
The vegetation flourishes and the fugitives return safely
challenge.explanation: The passage combines desolation, loss of goods, bloodshed, and danger from lions.
challenge.q: Which combination best shows the worsening calamity in these verses?

answers: The one who escapes from Moab and the remnant of the land
challenge.explanation: Verse 9 says that lions will come upon him that escapes of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
challenge.q: Who is threatened by the lions at the end of the passage?
